page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.32-256 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the 64-bit Arm architecture. The instance provides 64 dedicated physical cores powered by Ampere AmpereOne-M processors. Because each core executes exactly one hardware thread, all 64 vCPUs map directly to dedicated physical execution units without thread sharing. The system is provisioned with 256 GB of total system memory, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4 GB per core. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and contains no onboard GPU hardware.

A key architectural tradeoff for this instance is storage topology. The configuration includes no integrated local disks, meaning persistent storage, operating system volumes, and ephemeral caching layers must rely entirely on external network-attached block storage. Workloads demanding low-latency local disk access must factor in remote block performance. Conversely, the absence of simultaneous multithreading guarantees predictable CPU cycle availability across all 64 cores, avoiding execution contention typically associated with shared logical threads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high physical core density on the Arm architecture enables significant execution throughput for scale-out compute without the premium associated with hyper-threaded architectures. This balance of 64 independent execution units and 256 GB of memory is well configured for container orchestration clusters, large microservice meshes, continuous integration pipelines, web serving deployments, and distributed enterprise application backends.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.32-256 is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the 64-bit Arm Ampere AmpereOne-M architecture. It features 64 dedicated physical cores running one thread per core, ensuring each of the 64 vCPUs operates without simultaneous multithreading contention. The compute resources are paired with 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 4 GB per core allocation. The server includes no integrated local storage or discrete GPU accelerators, requiring all file storage and operating system images to utilize external network-attached block storage. Networking provision includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Providing consistent per-core execution and high thread capacity, this instance offers efficient resource scaling for parallel enterprise workloads such as container platforms, distributed application services, CI/CD runners, and high-concurrency web backends.
